history.summary: A small, ancient Shiva shrine standing just east of the Anantheshwara Temple on Car Street, within the Sri Krishna Matha complex in Udupi. According to the Madhva Vijaya it was originally called Moodu Devalaya (the eastern temple), and a longstanding custom — recorded by Vishvapati Tirtha's commentary — requires devotees to first salute Shiva at the eastern temple, then visit Anantheshwara, before proceeding to the Krishna Matha. Legend says the moon god Chandra performed penance here to free himself from Daksha's curse, and Shiva, pleased, appeared and blessed him — hence the name Chandramouleshwara ('the moon-crested lord'). The temple is built below ground level, approached by descending steps; local accounts say it was constructed over a filled-in tank or lake bed. Stone inscriptions in the temple date to the 11th or 12th century, while the architecture is placed in the 7th-8th century Alupa period. Some sources even derive the name 'Udupi' from this shrine, since 'Udupa' means 'lord of the stars/moon' — though scholars note this etymology developed recently and the name is likely of Tulu origin.

name: Chandramouleshwara Temple
town_description: Udupi is a coastal city in Tulu Nadu, Karnataka, best known as the birthplace of the Dvaita school of Vedanta and home to the famous Sri Krishna Matha. It is a major pilgrimage city whose temple streets draw lakhs of devotees, and it is also famous nationwide for Udupi vegetarian cuisine. Malpe beach lies about 6 km away, and the city is well connected by rail and road to Mangaluru and Bengaluru.
